title: Tweet Index
summary: Find the post you meant to come back to.
description: A local search tool for saved X likes and bookmarks, with meaning-based retrieval and model-assisted ranking.
problem: Saving is easy. Finding the right post months later is harder, especially when the useful idea is inside an image or a linked article.
approach: Five stages—Capture, Store, Enrich, Index, and Search—turn saved posts into searchable results. SQLite and embeddings are local; model enrichment and reranking send relevant content to API providers. Linked pages and images are fetched during enrichment.
outcome: The original recording shows one search run, including timing and cost. Its counts and measurements describe that recording, not guaranteed product performance.

title: R2D2
summary: Stay with the text. Go deeper.
description: A native Windows reading assistant that turns highlighted text into explanations, simpler wording, definitions, and key takeaways.

media.caption: Actual settings window from the R2D2 README.
Actual provider selector from the README; model availability can change.

problem: Switching away from a difficult passage interrupts reading. The assistant uses selected text as the context for a focused question.
approach: The source implements a WPF sidebar and a provider catalog across three API formats. Selected text, the question, and recent conversation turns are sent to the selected provider. Keys are stored in Windows Credential Manager. The README says OpenAI has received the most testing; other provider paths are less exercised.
outcome: The source code and settings screenshots document the workflow. OCR, visible conversation history, and a UI control for canceling an answer are not implemented in the inspected version.

title: Kurate
description: An easy-to-use content curation website for saving your favorite content from across the internet, with recommendations based on RSS feeds.
summary: A personal library for articles, videos, and podcasts, built with Claude Code.

problem: People save articles, videos, and podcasts across the web, then lose the thread. Kurate brings that material into a personal library.
approach: The existing portfolio documents React, Node.js, Cloudflare D1 storage, and React Native / Expo mobile work. RSS feeds support content recommendations.
outcome: The supplied screenshots show the landing experience and a curated library; no usage or retention results are supplied.

title: AI-paper explanation skill
summary: From a dense paper to an idea you can use.
description: A Claude Code skill that turns AI research papers into interactive HTML lessons with analogies, workflows, annotated code, plain-English math, and quizzes.

media.caption: Actual lesson output from the ai-paper-skill README — Attention Is All You Need, view 1.

problem: Readers want to understand the ideas behind AI papers without losing the detail inside equations, architecture diagrams, and terminology.
approach: The skill guides a coding assistant to analyze a paper and produce a self-contained HTML lesson. Teaching patterns include analogies, annotated code, equation explanations, and scenario-based quizzes. Inspired by Zara Zhang’s codebase-to-course skill, as credited in the original LinkedIn post; this project specializes in research papers.
outcome: The README includes example output for Attention Is All You Need. The interactive lesson on this page was written for the portfolio to illustrate the skill’s teaching patterns; it was not generated by running the skill.

title: CommandVoice
summary: Speak a thought. Keep your workflow.
description: A Python desktop core for hotkey-triggered recording, faster-whisper transcription, clipboard delivery, and optional pasting into the active window.
problem: Typing can interrupt the flow of a thought. A desktop dictation tool can turn speech into text where the user is already working.
approach: The public source registers start and stop hotkeys, records audio, runs faster-whisper locally, and copies the transcript before optionally synthesizing a paste. Automatic model selection chooses base or large-v3 according to hardware. Model files may be downloaded; the inspected transcription path does not call a hosted speech API.
outcome: The public repository exposes a console-driven Python core. Its README mentions an independent Electron UI, but the UI and installers are not included. The illustration represents the verified core workflow, not a screenshot of that UI.

title: Orbit PRM
summary: Remember the conversation. Make the next one count.
description: A professional relationship manager for contact ingestion, conversation summaries, relationship warmth, enrichment, and follow-up reminders.
problem: Professional relationships span email, meetings, and long gaps. Remembering the context and the next commitment becomes its own job.
approach: The code stores records in local SQLite, syncs with Google services, and sends interaction content to OpenAI for summaries. Enrichment sends contact identifiers to Exa and uses OpenAI for extraction and optional web search. Local storage does not mean all processing stays on the device.
outcome: The public source implements ingestion, summaries, warmth scoring, enrichment, and reminders. This case study uses fictional contacts only; no private database or correspondence is included.

title: LinkedIn Attribution System
description: An attribution prototype that helps go-to-market and sales teams interpret engagement with LinkedIn posts and prioritize follow-up actions. Built with Codex.
summary: A campaign attribution prototype for go-to-market teams running LinkedIn programs.

media.caption: Original attribution prototype dashboard for engagement and account context.
Original workflow diagram: engagement data, account mapping, intent, and pipeline paths.

technology: LinkedIn API, Exa API, OpenAI API
problem: GTM and sales teams need to connect LinkedIn engagement to account context and useful next actions.
approach: The repository documents ingestion, enrichment, scoring, account mapping, and next-best actions. The portfolio lists React + Vite, Python, LinkedIn, Exa, and OpenAI APIs. Engagement signals support prioritization; they do not prove causation. The public README identifies PostgreSQL storage and mock/CSV ingestion alongside an API scaffold; it does not establish a production LinkedIn integration.
outcome: Screenshots and a workflow diagram are available. No revenue lift or conversion result is established.
